title: Thyroid Gland Anatomy: Lobes, Follicles & Laryngeal Map
description: Study thyroid gland anatomy in the anterior neck, including the right and left lobes, isthmus, colloid follicles, parathyroid glands, and laryngeal nerves.
h1: Thyroid Gland Anatomy: Lobes, Follicles, Parathyroids and Nerves
blurb: Wrapped like a butterfly around the upper trachea, thyroid follicles store iodinated thyroglobulin colloid to pace basal metabolism, with four parathyroids behind.
lead: Shaped like a butterfly wrapped around the upper windpipe, the thyroid gland stores its own hormone supply inside microscopic colloid spheres called follicles. In this illustrated guide to thyroid gland anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including right lobe, left lobe, isthmus, pyramidal lobe—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Shaped like a butterfly wrapped around the upper windpipe, the thyroid gland stores its own hormone supply inside microscopic colloid spheres called follicles. The thyroid is built from follicles — spheres of cuboidal cells filled with colloid, a store of thyroglobulin. Iodide is trapped, oxidised and attached to tyrosine residues to make T3 and T4, released under control of pituitary TSH. These hormones raise basal metabolic rate, oxygen consumption and heat production, and are essential for growth and brain development. Parafollicular C cells secrete calcitonin. Embedded behind the gland, the four parathyroid glands sense calcium and release parathyroid hormone — the minute-to-minute controller of plasma calcium. Within the human body, the thyroid gland (Glandula thyroidea) is situated in anterior neck, C5–T1, in front of trachea and larynx, receives arterial perfusion via superior & inferior thyroid arteries (± thyroidea ima), and is innervated by sympathetic + parasympathetic (vasomotor only; secretion is TSH-driven).

The right lobe (Lobus dexter) is one of two lateral lobes, 5–8 cm long, lying against the trachea and oesophagus and covered by the pretracheal fascia. Physiologically, the right lobe secretes T3/T4 from its follicles. The left lobe (Lobus sinister) is the mirror-image lobe; asymmetry between lobes is common and usually benign. Physiologically, the left lobe secretes T3/T4. The isthmus is the bridge crossing the 2nd–4th tracheal rings, joining the two lobes. Physiologically, the isthmus connects the lobes into a single gland. The pyramidal lobe (Lobus pyramidalis) is a tongue of thyroid tissue ascending toward the hyoid in ~50% of people, a remnant of the thyroglossal duct. Physiologically, the pyramidal lobe governs functionally ordinary thyroid tissue. The trachea & larynx (Trachea et larynx) is the gland wraps the airway; the cricoid cartilage and thyroid cartilage lie above. Physiologically, the trachea & larynx governs anatomical landmark and the reason goitres cause compressive symptoms. The thyroid arteries (Arteriae thyroideae) are superior thyroid (from external carotid) and inferior thyroid (from thyrocervical trunk), with rich anastomoses. Physiologically, the thyroid arteries governs give the gland its extremely high blood flow per gram.

Clinically, regarding the right lobe, an enlarging lobe can compress the trachea (stridor) or the recurrent laryngeal nerve (hoarseness). From a diagnostic standpoint, in the left lobe, a dominant nodule in one lobe is investigated with ultrasound and, if suspicious, fine-needle cytology. In clinical pathology involving the isthmus, it is the landmark for emergency tracheostomy and cricothyroidotomy is performed above it. Medical evaluation of the pyramidal lobe also notes that if left behind at thyroidectomy it can hypertrophy and mimic a recurrent goitre or a midline neck mass.

questions.question: Where is the thyroid gland located?
questions.answer: The thyroid has two lateral lobes joined by an isthmus in the front of the neck, close to the larynx and upper trachea.

questions.question: What do thyroid follicles make?
questions.answer: Follicular cells use iodine and stored thyroglobulin in colloid to produce thyroid hormones. Nearby parafollicular cells produce calcitonin.

questions.question: What is the isthmus?
questions.answer: The thyroid isthmus is the narrow bridge crossing the second to fourth tracheal rings and joining the two lobes.

questions.question: Where are the larynx and trachea located?
questions.answer: The larynx lies above the trachea in the neck; the trachea descends from the larynx through the neck into the thorax.

questions.question: What do thyroid follicles and colloid do?
questions.answer: Thyroid follicles synthesize and store thyroid hormone in colloid; thyroid-stimulating hormone promotes iodine uptake and hormone production and release.
